query: Single-phase high-entropy alloys have difficulty achieving a satisfactory strength–ductility balance. Earlier work introduced the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure to enable large-sized production and obtain good strength and plasticity, but its performance still falls short of industrial requirements. Its use in aircraft and spacecraft fasteners further requires stability under extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosion, while relevant creep and corrosion studies remain limited by sample-size and experimental-environment constraints. Given these limitations and design requirements, what single intervention could improve the alloy’s practical performance? Present one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted improvement over the starting material, boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a feasible experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a minor addition of niobium (Nb) to the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy will improve its strength–ductility balance as well as its high-temperature stability including creep resistance and corrosion performance.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure currently exhibiting suboptimal strength–ductility balance and limited high-temperature performance.
generation.intervention: Modify the alloy composition by adding approximately 2 wt.% Nb during alloy synthesis.
generation.conditions: The modified alloy is processed under conditions similar to the baseline (e.g., casting and heat-treatment processes optimized for the eutectic structure), and performance is evaluated under industrial-relevant conditions including cyclic temperature fluctuations, room-temperature creep loading, and corrosive environments.
generation.structural_mediator: The Nb addition is expected to induce the formation of fine, Nb-rich precipitates along the lamellar interfaces, which can pin interface motion.
generation.mechanism: Nb-rich precipitates reduce dislocation mobility and inhibit coarsening of the eutectic lamellae. This precipitate pinning mechanism enhances the strength and ductility balance by retarding deformation processes (including creep) and improving resistance to corrosion-related degradation at high temperatures.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Nb-modified alloy will demonstrate an increased yield strength and improved ductility relative to the baseline, accompanied by enhanced creep resistance and better stability under cyclic temperature fluctuations. Improvements are expected to be significant enough to bring the alloy closer to industrial requirements for aerospace fasteners.
generation.baseline: The original AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy exhibits a fine lamellar structure with acceptable but suboptimal strength-ductility balance and limited performance under high-temperature, mechanical, and corrosive stresses.
generation.boundary: The proposed improvement is expected to hold under industrial conditions pertinent to aircraft and spacecraft fasteners (e.g., wide temperature fluctuations, sustained mechanical loading, and corrosive environments). However, the benefits may be diminished if the Nb addition leads to the formation of detrimental phases or if processing parameters are significantly altered.
generation.uncertainty: While Nb is predicted to refine the microstructural features and improve mechanical properties, the exact optimum concentration and long-term stability of the Nb-induced precipitates are uncertain. There is also a risk that excessive Nb could cause embrittlement or adversely affect corrosion behavior.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set with the baseline AlCoCrFeNi2.1 composition and a second set with the addition of ~2 wt.% Nb. Ensure identical processing (casting, heat-treatment, etc.) for both sets. Subject all samples to mechanical testing (tensile and creep tests) and accelerated corrosion testing under simulated cyclic temperature fluctuations representative of aerospace service conditions.
measurements: Yield strength and ultimate tensile strength
Ductility (percent elongation or reduction in area)
Creep rate under sustained load at room and elevated temperatures
Corrosion rates and surface degradation under accelerated conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Nb-modified alloy does not exhibit statistically significant improvements (e.g., >10% increase in yield strength and ductility combined, and improved creep resistance and corrosion performance) compared to the baseline alloy under the specified test conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
